newsitem.title: ITALY: Hard-hitting US director plans "Dolce Vita" remake.
newsitem.headline: Hard-hitting US director plans "Dolce Vita" remake.

text.p: Independent U.S. film director Abel Ferrara, whose hard-hitting films include "The Driller Killer" and "Bad Lieutenant", said on Tuesday he was planning a remake of the classic Italian movie "La Dolce Vita".
"I'll remake "La Dolce Vita" and (Marcello) Mastroianni will work for me," Italian news agency AGI quoted Ferrara as telling a film festival on the Mediterranean island of Capri.
Mastroianni starred as the suave reporter hero of Federico Fellini's 1960 cult tale of the decadent Rome high life, one of the most famous Italian films of all time.

Ferrara told Pascal Vicedomini, artistic director of the "Capri, Hollywood 1996" festival by telephone from Miami where he is finishing his latest film, "The Blackout", that the Dolce Vita project was "particularly dear" and he was already at work.
"It's a great challenge to follow in the footsteps of a director whom I adore, Federico Fellini," AGI quoted him as saying. "I'm already looking at the screenplay."
But Ferrara said he planned to give Mastroianni only a cameo role as the father of the hero.
Neither Mastroianni nor the festival organisers could immediately be reached for comment.
